drivingQuestion: Why do those ascending for the three upper rites not circle the altar?

segments.he: כׇּל הָעוֹלִים לְמִזְבֵּחַ, מַאי טַעְמָא? אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: נְסָכִים – שֶׁמָּא יִתְעַשְּׁנוּ, וְעוֹלַת הָעוֹף – שֶׁמָּא תָּמוּת בֶּעָשָׁן.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that «everyone who ascends» the ramp «to the altar» ascends via the right side of the ramp, circles the altar until reaching the southwest corner, and descends via the left side of the ramp, with the exception of one ascending in order to perform the wine or water libations, or to sacrifice a bird burnt offering on the southwest corner of the altar. In those cases the priest would ascend directly to the southwest corner. The Gemara asks: «What is the reason» for these exceptions to the standard practice? «Rabbi Yoḥanan says:» With regard to the «libations,» the priest would not walk all the way around the altar «lest» the wine or water «absorb» the «smoke» of the altar fire. «And» with regard to «a bird burnt offering» he would not walk all the way around «lest» the bird «die from» inhaling «the smoke.»

moves.about: mishna lemma on the route of all who ascend

moves.summary: Smoke would spoil the libations and kill the bird.
